purpose: Section 25: results of the 16 required adversarial scenarios for the explicit claim-level safe-failure architecture.
result: 15/15 test cases pass (covering all 16 required scenarios - two scenario groups, 7/8/10 and 12/16, are combined into single test cases each because they exercise the same code path with the same real-database assertions).

scenarioDisposition.scenario: material claim compiles successfully -> no failure event
material claim cannot compile -> explicit review event
sibling claim warning does not cover target claim
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: Two distinct semanticUnitIds (6.01(a) vs 6.01(b)) produce two distinct ClaimReviewItem rows; checkExplicitSafeFailure for claim A never matches claim B's item.

scenarioDisposition.scenario: generic section-level warning does not cover target claim
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: Same mechanism as #7 - claim identity is anchor-derived, never section-level-generic.

scenarioDisposition.scenario: two pipeline failures for same claim aggregate correctly
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: recordClaimReview called twice for the same claimKey with different (stage, reasonCode) produces ONE item with 2 observations, outcome OBSERVATION_APPENDED on the second call.

scenarioDisposition.scenario: two genuinely distinct sibling claims remain distinct review items
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: Same test as #7 - explicitly asserts reviewItemId(A) !== reviewItemId(B).

scenarioDisposition.scenario: amendment supersedes unresolved historical claim appropriately
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: resolveClaimReview(action=SUPERSEDE) transitions status to SUPERSEDED with a ClaimReviewDecision row recording previousStatus=OPEN_REVIEW.

resolveClaimReview(action=ACCEPT, decidedBy=<real reviewer>) preserves all prior observations and the decision itself in ClaimReviewDecision; a later re-detection reopens (REOPEN decision row) without deleting the original ACCEPT decision row.

scenarioDisposition.scenario: tenant A event cannot satisfy tenant B claim
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: checkExplicitSafeFailure(companyB, sameClaimKey) returns claimSpecificReviewEventExists=false - the (companyId, claimKey) unique constraint means tenant B's own row, if any, is entirely independent.

scenarioDisposition.scenario: document A definition problem cannot satisfy document B claim
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: semanticUnitId's own upstream computation (computeSemanticUnitId) folds documentId into its content hash, so two real distinct-document units never produce the same semanticUnitId/claimKey in the first place - verified directly, and the adversarial same-raw-id construction is documented as an intentionally out-of-scope edge case (see test file comment) since it cannot arise from the real computation.

scenarioDisposition.scenario: non-material harmless diagnostic does not create a user-facing review event
scenarioDisposition.mechanism: materiality gate (CRITICAL/MATERIAL only) - INFORMATIONAL and REVIEW_UNCERTAIN both return null regardless of coverageState.
Same test as #12 - sourceEvidence/sourceCitation asserted unchanged after ACCEPT resolution.

additionalTestsBeyondTheRequired16: Idempotent re-recording of an identical observation (ALREADY_RECORDED, no duplicate row) - proves the architecture is safe to call on every pipeline re-run without unbounded growth.
No-anchor unit fails closed (returns null rather than fabricating a documentId) - a defensive test for a case that should not occur in practice but must never corrupt a foreign key if it does.
regressionProtection: This new test file adds to, never replaces, the existing tests/contract-model/semantic-coverage-*.test.ts suite (18 files) which this architecture's derive.ts/integrate.ts consume as an unmodified upstream dependency - see 20-test-quality-gates.json for the full-suite confirmation that none of those pre-existing tests changed behavior.
